rationale: Roberts is most likely to keep the assignment and write a Boyle-anchored, conduct-specific preemption opinion rejecting categorical “combatant-activities preemption” untethered to concrete military direction. The three dissenters are likely to splinter between a Thomas/Alito-style structural-conflict dissent and a narrower Kavanaugh dissent, while one or more majority justices may concur to emphasize either textual limits on federal common law or the need for a functional-equivalent-to-directive test.
